codex_contract.preserved_semantics: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives the real user surface, records observable evidence, and hands maintenance to a verification loop.

native_mapping.fallback: Missing harness, broken startup, or unavailable native surface preserves the source and returns a blocked verification result.
native_mapping.availability: renderer, real disposable CLI verification fixture, project-local .agents/skills/verify-<app>/ structure, captured stdout/stderr/exit evidence, explicit cleanup ownership, and unsafe-input guards checked; live target application, full harness, and syntax/version doctor not supplied
native_mapping.routing_authority: proof-orchestrator selects the proof path; model-capability-router remains the standing model authority

external_dependencies: target application runtime or supplied harness
permission_gates: Write only to an explicit project-local .agents/skills/verify-<app>/ destination; never write a global skill from this flow.
Run the generated instructions only against an instance started by the verification run, and never kill by process name.
Missing harness or broken startup preserves the source and fails verification.
Do not publish, open a PR, or mutate product code as part of generation without separate explicit authorization.

behavioral_proof.positive: A disposable Python CLI subprocess drives a notes create flow, captures stdout/stderr/exit and regular-file side effects, then creates a project-local .agents/skills/verify-<app>/ with Launch/Doctor/Drive/Evidence/Cleanup/Helpers, a feature-map README, required feature headings, and persisted JSON evidence. Cleanup removes only explicit app state and preserves evidence; the result remains `FIXTURE_ONLY` because no live target application is driven.
behavioral_proof.missing_tool_or_input: Isolated fixture returns blocked when the verification app is unavailable and performs no product edit.
behavioral_proof.error: The CLI fixture blocks when the app is unavailable, a declared cleanup path pre-exists, or a feature/app slug is unsafe; subprocess evidence mismatch returns an explicit error before writing the skill. The doctor is only an existence/non-symlink check, and live startup/target health remains unproven.

upstream_readme.note: Verified in the pinned upstream clone; the README is referenced for provenance and is not vendored in this skills-only snapshot.

security_review.decision: Keep the source finding and provenance; do not dismiss it because the adapter adds a warning.

codex_note:
## Codex adaptation boundary

This mirror uses the native Codex project-local skill root `.agents/skills/verify-<app>/`. It discovers the real surface from the repository, selects the proof path through proof-orchestrator, and respects the selected model and effort through model-capability-router. The native verification runner is required for a verified result. If the harness or startup is missing, preserve the project and report `blocked`. Generation never installs a global skill, publishes an artifact, opens a PR, kills by process name, or changes product code. The feature-map references intentionally retain the reproducible upstream `control-notes` commands; adapt them to concrete commands observed in the target repository before use. Map browser/Electron/web actions to `cursor-control-ui`, and CLI/TUI actions to `cursor-control-cli`, only when those skills are installed and applicable; otherwise record the exact surface gap. The bounded CLI fixture uses separate subprocesses, captures stdout/stderr/exit plus regular-file side effects, writes only the explicit project-local skill tree, and keeps app-state writes/isolated filesystem status honest. Its minimum doctor checks file existence/non-symlink only; it does not claim syntax, version, live target, or native host verification.
codex_rule: Respect native Codex model/effort, permissions and actual tool availability; no automatic Cursor runtime equivalence.
preserved_requirement: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, "make a control skill for this repo", or when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior.
proof: Pinned source hash and deterministic renderer are static provenance. Focused tests render the held candidate and run a disposable Python CLI subprocess to create `.agents/skills/verify-notes/` with the required skill sections, feature README/headings, captured stdout/stderr/exit evidence, explicit cleanup path, and persisted JSON. The test performs the minimum doctor check, preserves evidence after removing `notes.json`, rejects pre-existing cleanup state and unsafe names, introduces controlled feature drift, persists maintenance before/after evidence, reconciles it, and passes a second clean execution. Filesystem/network isolation, syntax/version doctor, live harness, target application, and native host activation remain unproven; result remains `FIXTURE_ONLY`.
reason: The adapter changes the generated destination and tool boundary while leaving the pinned upstream source unchanged.
